message.reasoning:
I'm planning a thorough JUnit 4 test suite for the Base64 class, starting by mapping out the constructors and their branching logic around line separators and line lengths that I'll need to cover.

I also need to trace through all the other methods to test: URL-safe checks, buffer resizing, encode/decode logic with their EOF and modulus branches, validation helpers like isBase64 and containsBase64Byte, and the various static convenience methods for encoding and decoding.

I'm continuing to map out coverage cases across the remaining decode/encode variants, whitespace handling, exception paths for non-byte-array inputs, and the BigInteger conversion helpers with their bit-length edge cases.

Since toIntegerBytes and other package-private methods need direct access, I'll place the test class in the same package so it can reach internal helpers like decode/encode with offsets, hasData, avail, readResults, setInitialBuffer, discardWhitespace, and toIntegerBytes directly. Then I'm outlining the constructor test methods, covering default construction, url-safe flags, and line-length behavior including rounding to multiples of four and zero-length edge cases.

Beyond that I'm sketching tests for null line separators forcing lineLength to zero, invalid separators containing base64 characters throwing exceptions, and checks for isUrlSafe, hasData/avail defaults, basic encode/decode roundtrips, empty and null array handling, padding behavior for one and two leftover bytes, url-safe encoding without padding, chunked encoding with line separators, whitespace tolerance during decode, isBase64/isArrayByteBase64 validation across valid, invalid, empty and whitespace inputs, and decodeObject overloads for byte arrays, strings, and invalid types.

I continue outlining tests covering encodeObject variants, encode/decodeToString, static Base64 helper methods, exceeding max result size, discarding whitespace, integer encode/decode including null-argument NPE, converting BigInteger to bytes across edge cases, buffer reuse and resizing, and large-data round trips that exercise internal buffer growth.

Now I'm planning the actual test implementation, starting with the BigInteger-to-bytes conversion logic and figuring out the bit-length edge case where a value's bit length is an exact multiple of eight, which trims the leading byte.

I'm working through several BigInteger examples like zero, one, and 255, tracing through the bit-length math to figure out exactly what byte array each should produce so I can write assertions that match the real behavior.

Now planning the test cases: constructor validation with non-multiple-of-4 line lengths, rejecting base64 characters as line separators, and decoding malformed input with non-base64 characters that should just get ignored.

I'm also mapping out edge cases for isBase64 with byte values, since bytes are signed and any value above 127 wraps negative, so I need to be careful about what values actually reach the check versus wrap around before then.

Then I move to verifying padding cases for single-byte and two-byte inputs: encoding "M" should yield "TQ==" by manually tracing the bit groupings, and I'm doing the same manual check for "Ma" to confirm it should produce a result ending in a single "=" pad.

Now I want to test three-byte input like "Man" which needs no padding at all, then plan a test for chunked encoding with a longer byte array that forces line-separator insertion when the encoded length exceeds the 76-character line limit.

I'm designing a test with exactly 57 input bytes so the encoded output lands precisely at 76 characters, which triggers the boundary case for line-separator insertion at end-of-stream. Beyond that, I want to verify roundtrip correctness across many sizes—0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 100, 1000 bytes—covering chunked/unchunked and URL-safe/standard variants.

I should also test with a large input around 20000 bytes to force the internal buffer to resize multiple times, exercising the doubling logic in resizeBuffer, though directly testing the package-private readResults path when the buffer is reused might be tricky since it's only invoked internally.

Since the test class shares the same package, I can actually call hasData(), avail(), readResults(), and setInitialBuffer() directly for extra branch coverage — checking hasData() is false initially and true after encoding, verifying avail()'s behavior, confirming readResults() returns the right value when buffer is null, and testing setInitialBuffer() with a null output has no effect.

I'll also test setInitialBuffer() when the output length mismatches outAvail (no effect) versus matches (buffer gets set), then move to encode/decode edge cases — calling encode twice with eof already set to hit the early-return branch, and decoding a byte array starting with a PAD character to trigger the break-on-PAD logic and verify the modulus check afterward.

I want to add a test for decoding a lone PAD character, expecting an empty result array, plus a test mixing valid base64 with junk characters like "!!" and newlines to exercise the branches for out-of-range bytes and ignored characters. I'm also checking isBase64 against a byte value that overflows to negative when cast, and thinking through how to hit the branch where a positive value exceeds the decode table length.

I should also cover the exception branches for decode(Object) and encode(Object), test encodeBase64 with a maxResultSize that triggers IllegalArgumentException, verify encodeInteger(null) throws NullPointerException, and test decodeInteger. Now I'm putting together the full test file with the necessary imports.
